title: Choose the visual world for druyn.com
question: The roll assigned Werkplan (the timber shop-drawing set). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Werkplan
options.lineage: Swiss timber-construction shop drawings (Abbundplan / Werkplan): bordered sheets, dimension chains, title block, blueprint cover
options.thesis: The site is a drawing set: every section is a numbered sheet, the plan-execute-forecast loop is drawn as the engineering drawing it is, and the title block never leaves the corner.
options.viewport: Sheet 1 is the blueprint cover: the headline in condensed grotesk sits on a dimension chain top-left; right, a white line drawing of a real project (Projektstart, Standortanalyse, Vorprojekt, Behördeneingabe) with booked hours as dimension figures in red, drawing itself on load; bottom-right the Plankopf (title block) carries project, sheet 1/6, scale 1:1 and the primary action 'Interesse anmelden' as the red approval stamp. Scrolling turns sheets; the Plankopf stays pinned and counts Blatt 2/6, 3/6 as navigation.
options.risk: Can read as a cold CAD export if the lettering is timid or the drawing is decoration; the drawing must be a true drawing of the loop with real demo numbers.

raised.raise: No unpainted area: every region of every sheet is owned by the drawing grammar; no neutral template gaps between sections.
One shared order over many voices: each sheet has its own drawing, the pinned Plankopf is the only navigation, and on phones the nearest sheet's title block stays dominant.
Type behaves as matter: dimension figures are the display scale and headlines sit on measured chains, not floating over a background.
Layout snaps to whole drawing modules, never fractional ones, and line work draws itself on reveal like glaze filling the lines.
One strict sheet grid is the entire composition; captions, screenshots and controls live inside the same zones (A–D / 1–8).
State is a mark, not a hue: done tasks get a drawn check, today gets a flag, and the blueprint blue owns a third of the scroll (cover, pricing, close), never a sticker.

options.label: Wegweiser
options.lineage: Swiss yellow hiking signposts with hour estimates, white-red-white trail bands, Swisstopo map
options.thesis: The forecast is a signpost: every destination with a realistic time, recalculated as you walk.
options.viewport: A tall signpost cluster fills the left: the top blade is the headline, the blades below are real project phases with their computed hours (Vorprojekt 0/36 h, Behördeneingabe 0/20 h, Fundation KW 36). Right, the product's planning view as the map. Primary action is a black plate on the post.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category would land on for a Swiss planning tool; instantly legible, but tourism cheer can undercut engineering seriousness.

options.label: Cutting bench select rail
options.lineage: film editor's bench: perforated rail, punched frames, tape flags
options.thesis: Every project phase as a punched frame on one orange rail; where you stopped is a folded flag.
options.viewport: A perforated rail crossing the viewport with phases as frames, trims hanging on pins below.
options.risk: A film bench is nobody's workplace in a Swiss engineering office.
options.case: Fuses on clarity (frames as phases, marks as state) but Swiss planners do not identify with a cutting room; loses both axes to the drawing set.
options.kept: State is a mark not a hue; one colour owns a third of the screen.

options.label: Azulejo station hall
options.thesis: The product story painted in cobalt across a tile grid whose seams run through every scene.
options.viewport: A sixty-tile narrative panel of the planning loop over the doorway, captions in cartouches.
options.risk: Reads as a travel page, not a planning tool.
options.case: Beautiful discipline but no identification for engineers; product clarity drops once screenshots must become paintings.
options.kept: Whole-module layout snapping; line work fills itself on reveal.

options.label: Alphabet storm
options.thesis: Letters condense into the plan and break into weather when reality changes.
options.viewport: One word-weather event: PLAN rains into PROGNOSE across a white field.
options.risk: Spectacle without the product; forecast becomes metaphor instead of numbers.
options.case: Strong on type discipline, weak on both identification and clarity for a deterministic planning tool.
options.kept: Type as matter: dimension figures become the display scale.

options.label: ASCII live scene
options.thesis: The Gantt rendered as phosphor glyphs on one monospace grid.
options.viewport: A full-viewport glyph grid rendering the capacity chart live.
options.risk: Hacker aesthetic contradicts 'keine Black-Box-KI' and the warm product UI.
options.case: Terminal costume on a tool for engineers who do not live in terminals; loses both axes.
options.kept: One strict grid as the entire composition; rank by density not size.

options.label: Night-market sign river
options.lineage: temporary street signage, lanterns, handwritten boards
options.thesis: Each feature its own hand-painted stall sign along one river of lanterns.
options.viewport: A river of lantern-lit signs bending through the viewport toward the CTA.
options.risk: Loud and improvised where the product promises calm and precision.
options.case: The opposite of Swiss precision; loses both axes.
options.kept: One shared order across many voices; nearest sign dominant on phones.

options.label: Lowbrow gallery panel
options.thesis: The features as outlined figures fighting for one lacquered board.
options.viewport: A crowded lacquered tableau with a hand-lettered title panel across the base.
options.case: No identification, no clarity; loses both axes.
options.kept: No unpainted area: total commitment to one grammar.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The SaaS landing page every planning tool ships: centred headline, product screenshot in a browser frame, three feature cards, pricing table, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Pill badge, two-line centred headline, subcopy, two buttons, screenshot below the fold line.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Asana, Monday and every competitor by design.
